title: Etale complex class descent
statement: Let $I$ be a small cofiltered category, $D:I\to\mathrm{Sch}$ a diagram of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] with affine transitions, and $X=\varprojlim D$ with projections $f_i$. Let $\mathcal F_i^\bullet$ be complexes of abelian etale sheaves [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves] with unital compatible transitions $f_{ji}^{-1}\mathcal F_i^\bullet\to\mathcal F_j^\bullet$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], using the canonical composition isomorphisms [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition]. Suppose one integer $a$ satisfies $\mathcal F_i^n=0$ for all $i$ and $n<a$. Set $\mathcal F^\bullet=\varinjlim_i f_i^{-1}\mathcal F_i^\bullet$ termwise, and fix $p\in\mathbf Z$. Cohomology and its canonical maps are defined by derived global sections [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]. Every $x\in H^p(X,\mathcal F^\bullet)$ has a representative $y\in H^p(X_i,\mathcal F_i^\bullet)$ at some stage $i$, whose canonical pullback followed by the colimit complex map equals $x$.

proof.text: Apply graded class descent to obtain a finite decreasing filtration S of the target group, whole at 0 and zero at N=(p+1-a).toNat, with representatives modulo each next step.

Induct on k<=N to represent every element of S_(N-k). At k=0 the element is zero, represented by zero at any stage (the cofiltered category is nonempty). At k+1 choose a graded representative y at stage i, apply the induction hypothesis to the residual x-B_i(y) in the next step, then use filteredness of I opposite to move y and the residual representative to one stage. Cocone naturality and additivity show that their sum represents x. At k=N, S_0 is the whole target.
